messages:
Priya: Helix12B int6 bring-up — quick econ + quality snapshot. TL;DR: int6 gives the best token cost but shows regressions on longform summarization. Need product/GTN guidance on routing defaults and canary plan.

Sam: Can you drop the concrete perf + cost numbers so we can model unit economics?

Priya: Sure — short bench notes (512-token chat slices on our standard harness):
```
Helix12B fp16 baseline: p95=95ms, cost ~ $0.45 / 1k tokens
Helix12B int8: p95=110ms, cost ~ $0.26 / 1k tokens
Helix12B int6: p95=135ms, cost ~ $0.18 / 1k tokens
Throughput (tokens/sec) scales similarly; int6 has slightly higher CPU postproc overhead causing p95 tail to worsen.
```
Estimates are host-cost normalized (gpu+infra). Variance +/-10% depending on sequence length.

Alex: Thanks. Where are the quality deltas? any signal on hallucination / instruction-following?

Priya: Short summary:
- Bench eval (400-sample summarization set, >1k token sources): fp16 baseline median ROUGE-L = 42.1
- int8 median ROUGE-L = 41.6 (~ -0.5)
- int6 median ROUGE-L = 39.2 (~ -2.9)
Qualitative: int6 drops on referential cohesion and entity linking in long contexts. For short chat turns (<128 tokens) the delta is <0.3 and usually acceptable.

Maya: Product note: most GTN chat traffic is short multi-turns (avg 80 tokens). For those flows, int6 could be a big win on cost. But features that generate long summaries or code should stick to int8 or fp16.

Jordan: Proposed routing rules (initial):
- user_chat_short (<=128 tokens): Helix12B-int6
- user_chat_long (>128 tokens) OR code/summarization routes: Helix12B-int8
- fallback: fp16 for safety if we detect quality regression or high hallucination score
Also suggest a per-route flag to opt-out.

Priya: + add additional checks: automatic fallback when eval-signal drops by >1.5x baseline for a rolling 1h window or when user-visible error rate increases >0.5%.

Liam: For GTN materials I can draft a digest: recommended default = Helix12B-int8; cost optimization knob = enable int6 for short/low-risk flows. Want the 1M-token unit cost numbers for the blurb.

Priya: ballpark unit econ per 1M tokens (host normalized):
- fp16: ~$450
- int8: ~$260
- int6: ~$180
So switching eligible short-chat traffic to int6 vs int8 saves ~30% on token cost; vs fp16 ~60%.

Sam: Nice. What about latency SLO impact for interactive UI? p95 135ms for int6 is not great vs 95ms baseline. Can we mitigate?

Priya: Options:
- add small local caching of prefixes (helpful for multi-turns)
- micro-batching tweaks for short queries (reduce overhead)
- we can also limit int6 to non-interactive paths first (async completion, background generation).

Maya: Product preference: prefer conservative rollout — enable int6 behind an experiment first (5% traffic), measure CSAT / ERR / hallucination signals, then ramp.

Jordan: Canary plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 3 days if signals stable. Rollback triggers:
- quality (ROUGE/BLEU/ROUGE-L) drop > 1.0 absolute on eval slices, OR
- user-visible error/hallucination signal increase > 0.5% absolute, OR
- latency p95 increase > 50ms for interactive routes.

Priya: I'll push an ops checklist: config flags, metric dashboards (quality, hallucination proxy, latency tail, cost), and a small slice of manual evals (100 longform summaries) at canary.

eval-bot: Automated run complete — canary-slice (5% sample) results uploaded: https://internal/bench/helix12b/int6/canary-2024-07-13 — short-turn metrics look fine; longform regressions visible.

Liam: Great — I'll write the GTN blurb and include a short scorecard:
- Recommended default: Helix12B-int8 (best balance)
- Cost-optimization mode: Helix12B-int6 for short/low-risk flows (with canary + metrics)
- Rollout: 3-stage canary + automatic fallback rules (as above)

Alex: One more ask: add an explicit eval set for code-generation and instruction-following before wider rollouts. Int6 might be particularly bad for code.

Priya: Agreed. I'll add a code-specific slice and bump the manual checks.

Maya: SGTM. Thanks @Priya and team — this gives product the knobs we need. :thumbsup: 

Sam: Thanks — I'll update the cost model spreadsheet and tag the finance reviewer.

Liam: I'll post the GTN draft in #product-docs tomorrow.

Priya: Filing as action items: 1) ops checklist + dashboards 2) code & longform eval slices 3) GTN blurb draft 4) canary config. Assigning to @Liam/@Alex/@Priya.

Jordan: +1 — let's sync after the first canary results.

Priya: Ok closing this thread for now, will update with canary link.
